The only one that reads what a message means

Stoatmod's own AI, running on our hardware, checks messages for serious harm across categories such as hate, violent extremism, illegal activity and sexual content. It acts only when a category scores 90% or higher, and an optional Thinking check makes it double-check borderline cases and explain itself.

The widest rule-based toolkit

Kuma has the most complete set of rules: a tiered content filter that sees through leetspeak and look-alike letters, link checks against a threat feed, an anti-raid suite with lockdown and a waiting room, and cases with appeals. It doesn't use AI, so it matches patterns rather than reading meaning.

bronx is built mainly for fun: economy, gambling games, counting, levelling, custom commands and roleplay. Its moderation tools are real but light: ban, kick and timeout, a moderation history, a word and regex filter, simple anti-raid triggers and audit logs.
